agree.reason: The candid tone and the 20-to-12-hour redesign make a phone screen plausible, but a skeptical HR manager never sees evidence that this teacher already keeps audit-ready records, so her assumption is only partly shaken.

honest.reason: The claims stay within the facts, and the letter rightly drops the unsupported 'cut training in half' promise; the line that the newly trained teachers kept 'the same safety record' is a mild inference rather than a stated fact.

works_the_facts.reason: The raw numbers are repeated but never put in their strongest true form: a 40% cut in training time, a 17-point pass-rate gain, about 1,000 students trained without a serious injury, and roughly 12 teachers trained since 2020.

right_comparison.reason: The AP trend is given, but the real alternative, an experienced GMP trainer, is never set against what this candidate offers, apart from a general claim that teaching novices is the core of the job.

qualification.reason: The May 2 course date and the 90-day review are concrete and checkable, but nothing says what happens if they are missed, and the June 14 earliest start date is left out entirely.

objections.reason: The letter admits she has no GMP record-keeping experience but leaves out the facts that answer that objection: she keeps signed training records for every trainee, and two state audits of them found nothing.

fit.reason: It is a proper one-page cover letter addressed to the named manager, but it keeps name placeholders and omits interview availability and the start date that the application needs.
